title: Merchant pack
description: Brand -> spend-category facts for resolving a payment descriptor or e-receipt sender into a category the card engine can score. Editorial research, not observed network data: an MCC here is what a brand is BELIEVED to code as, and a consumer that scores on one must say so.

packVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. A consumer refuses a MAJOR it does not recognize rather than misreading a changed shape.

category.description: An engine category token. Not every value is scorable by the card catalogue (wholesaleClub is not); an unscorable category is still a true fact about the merchant and still belongs here.

matchKeys.description: Normalized needles (lowercase, diacritics folded, single-spaced) matched as whole words against a normalized merchant string. Ordered longest-first so the most specific needle wins.

emailDomains.description: Sender domains an e-receipt from this merchant arrives from. A far stronger key than any descriptor string: noreply@ubereats.com is unambiguous.

acceptanceProvenance.description: Where the narrowing of `acceptedNetworks` came from. Required only when the row is narrower than the open [amex, visa, mastercard] default, because the two directions are not the same claim: the open default is a NON-claim that costs a wrong owner one extra tap at the till, which they see and learn from, while removing a network is an affirmative negative claim the app renders as text ('does not accept American Express') and which silently withholds a card the owner may never discover they should have used. An unfalsifiable claim needs a falsifiable source. Same vocabulary as card-catalogue.schema.json's per-rule provenance, and like it, documentation-only: no decoder reads these keys, they gate the curator.

sourceType.description: `inferred` is deliberately absent. It is a legal value for an earn rate, where being wrong is visible in a statement; it is not one here, where the whole point of the gate is that a narrowing must rest on something a reviewer can open.

sources.description: The merchant's or issuer's own published page — a payment-methods, FAQ or help-centre URL. A blog, forum or aggregator is not a source for this claim.

lastVerifiedAt.description: The day a human last opened `sources` and read the claim there. Acceptance changes without announcement (Loblaw's own Amex position has moved), so a date is what makes the row ageable.

allOf.$comment: Narrowing below the open default requires provenance. Expressed as if/else rather than a direct 'is narrower' test because JSON Schema cannot compare an array to a default; 'contains all three' is the same predicate from the other side.
